draft.shortGloss: to arrive; to go to; up to
notes: Often used as a resultative complement after verbs of motion (走到, 跑到) or perception/search (看到, 听到, 找到) to show that a destination or goal was reached.
Common in the pattern 从…到… (from ... to/until ...) for both time and place.

senses.definition: To arrive at a place or reach a destination.

examples.translation: When will you arrive in Beijing?

senses.definition: To go to a place (usually followed by another verb).

examples.translation: I have to go to the office for a meeting tomorrow.

senses.definition: To reach a certain time, point, or extent (often after another verb or with 从).

examples.translation: The shop is open from morning until evening.

faults.why: Verb entry should be defined as a verb or complement, or note its prepositional function.
到 is also very common after perception/cognitive verbs (看到, 听到, 找到) to show successful completion.
